This notebook prepares one row per named estimated dog from the saved 2024 NYC license extract and matches full names against the selected SSA decades. It covers the dog/name portion of Barkonomics; geography, income comparisons and the other implementations remain separate work.

## Run this notebook
Open the repository as your editor workspace, start R in the repository root, and run the chunks from top to bottom. Later chunks use objects created earlier. To execute everything in a fresh R session and produce a self-contained HTML document, run `quarto render dog-names.qmd` from the repository root. Install Quarto and the R packages `tidyverse`, `knitr` and `rmarkdown` if they are not already available. Rendering uses the saved source files without downloading data.

The [source inventory](data/sources.csv) and [source documentation](data/README.md) describe the inputs. The [data dictionary](data/dog-name-data-dictionary.md) defines the output columns and table grains. ZIP codes and recorded birth years must be imported as text; CSV files do not preserve column types.

Read the row units as the workflow progresses: license record → estimated dog; annual name/sex count → name/decade → one name reference row → annotated estimated dog. `nrow()` counts table rows; `stopifnot()` stops execution when a required condition is false. Both are base R functions. Transformations use tidyverse verbs and native `|>` pipes. Codex assisted with implementation and checks.

## Prepare the data

### Load packages and inputs
```{r}
#| label: setup-and-source-inventory
library(tidyverse)

# Create the output folder if needed. recursive creates missing parent folders; showWarnings = FALSE avoids a warning when it already exists.
dir.create("data/derived", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Keep the source inventory available for inspecting provenance and future source use.
sources <- read_csv("data/sources.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

### Read the dog records and missing-name lookup
These are the input definitions, alongside the source inventory above. Read everything as text so literal NA, short ZIP codes and malformed birth years survive inspection. The raw CSV still has the published column names: `animalname`, `animalgender`, `animalbirth`, `breedname` and `zipcode`.

`missing_labels` reads our small, project-owned lookup of the six agreed missing-name labels. It is not another downloaded dataset or a previously cleaned dog table. The following join uses it to identify missing names while keeping `BABY`.

```{r}
#| label: read-source-records-as-text
dogs_raw <- read_csv(
  "data/raw/nyc-dogs-2024.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
  na = character(), trim_ws = FALSE
)
dogs_raw |>
  problems() |>
  nrow() -> dog_parsing_problem_count
stopifnot(dog_parsing_problem_count == 0)
dogs_raw |>
  nrow() -> source_dog_record_count
stopifnot(source_dog_record_count == 105974)
dogs_raw |>
  distinct(extract_year) |>
  pull(extract_year) -> observed_extract_years
stopifnot(observed_extract_years == "2024")

missing_labels <- read_csv(
  "data/lookups/missing_name_labels.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), na = character()
)
missing_labels |>
  count(recorded_name, name = "records_in_group") |>
  filter(records_in_group > 1) |>
  nrow() -> duplicated_missing_label_count
stopifnot(duplicated_missing_label_count == 0)
```

```{r}
#| label: read-source-records-as-text-preview
# n is the fixed dplyr argument for the number of rows, not a variable we named.
dogs_raw |>
  slice_head(n = 6)
```

### Label missing names
The lookup maps the six agreed labels to a common missing-name status. `BABY` is not in it. `rename()` changes column headers here for the first time, without changing their values: `new_name = published_name`. The `_original` suffix distinguishes preserved source values from the normalized name and ZIP columns created later.

```{r}
#| label: label-missing-names
dogs_raw |>
  mutate(source_row_id = row_number()) |>
  rename(
    name_original = animalname,
    sex = animalgender,
    birth_year = animalbirth,
    breed = breedname,
    zipcode_original = zipcode
  ) |>
  left_join(missing_labels, by = c("name_original" = "recorded_name"), relationship = "many-to-one") ->
  dogs_labeled
```

### Normalize formatting
Normalize full names, ZIP text and dates without changing recorded identity fields. `replace_na()` fills missing values with the stated default: an unmatched missing-label lookup means the name was recorded. Each chunk resumes the preceding table and saves its result on the right; the headings break up the explanation, not the direction of the transformations.

```{r}
#| label: normalize-formatting
dogs_labeled |>
  mutate(
    name_status = replace_na(name_status, "recorded"),
    name_missing = name_status == "not_recorded",
    name_key = str_to_upper(name_original, locale = "en"),
    zipcode_contains_one_to_five_digits = str_detect(zipcode_original, "^[0-9]{1,5}$"),
    zipcode_with_leading_zeros = str_pad(zipcode_original, width = 5, pad = "0"),
    license_issue_date = str_sub(licenseissueddate, 1, 10),
    license_expiry_date = str_sub(licenseexpireddate, 1, 10),
    extract_year = as.integer(extract_year),
    breed_label = str_trim(breed),
    birth_year_number = as.integer(birth_year)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    name_key = str_remove_all(name_key, "[\\s-]"),
    license_issue_date = parse_date(license_issue_date),
    license_expiry_date = parse_date(license_expiry_date),
    breed_label = str_to_upper(breed_label)
  ) ->
  dogs_formatted
```

```{r}
#| label: normalize-formatting-preview
dogs_formatted |>
  select(name_original, name_key, zipcode_original, license_issue_date) |>
  slice_head(n = 6)
```

### Flag uncertain fields
Flag missing names and uncertain identity fields before selecting estimated dogs.

```{r}
#| label: flag-uncertain-fields
dogs_formatted |>
  mutate(
    name_key = if_else(name_missing, NA_character_, name_key),
    compound_name = !name_missing & str_detect(name_original, "\\S\\s+\\S|[^\\s-]-[^\\s-]"),
    zipcode = if_else(zipcode_contains_one_to_five_digits, zipcode_with_leading_zeros, zipcode_original),
    zipcode_padded = zipcode != zipcode_original,
    zipcode_invalid = !str_detect(zipcode, "^[0-9]{5}$"),
    breed_unknown = breed_label %in% c("", "UNKNOWN"),
    birth_year_has_four_digits = str_detect(birth_year, "^[0-9]{4}$"),
    birth_year_in_range = between(birth_year_number, 1990L, 2024L),
    birth_year_suspect = !birth_year_has_four_digits | !birth_year_in_range,
    birth_year_suspect = replace_na(birth_year_suspect, TRUE),
    sex_unknown = !sex %in% c("F", "M")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    identity_uncertain = breed_unknown | birth_year_suspect | sex_unknown | zipcode_invalid
  ) ->
  dogs_clean
dogs_clean |>
  nrow() -> cleaned_license_count
stopifnot(cleaned_license_count == source_dog_record_count)
dogs_clean |>
  select(license_issue_date, license_expiry_date) |>
  anyNA() -> dates_have_missing_values
stopifnot(dates_have_missing_values == FALSE)
```

### Select named records
Missing-name records stay in the raw data and the audit, outside the named-dog denominator.

```{r}
#| label: select-named-records
dogs_clean |>
  filter(!name_missing) ->
  dogs_named
```

### Estimate individual dogs
Count each five-field group once. Unknown breed and suspect birth years remain literal key values. Latest means issue date; ties use expiry date, then the lowest row number in the fixed snapshot.

```{r}
#| label: estimate-individual-dogs
dog_key <- c("name_key", "sex", "birth_year", "breed", "zipcode")
dogs_named |>
  group_by(name_key, sex, birth_year, breed, zipcode) |>
  mutate(
    license_record_count = n(),
    original_name_variants = n_distinct(name_original),
    any_compound_name = any(compound_name),
    latest_issue_date = max(license_issue_date),
    latest_issue_ties = sum(license_issue_date == latest_issue_date)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(license_issue_date), desc(license_expiry_date), source_row_id, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    retained_row_label = str_pad(source_row_id, width = 6, pad = "0"),
    estimated_dog_id = str_c("dog2024-", retained_row_label)
  ) |>
  arrange(source_row_id) ->
  dogs_estimated
```

```{r}
#| label: estimate-individual-dogs-preview
dogs_estimated |>
  select(estimated_dog_id, name_original, license_record_count) |>
  slice_head(n = 6)
```

### Read the selected SSA years
Read the same thirty SSA files for broad recognition and the three top-100 lists.

```{r}
#| label: read-the-selected-ssa-years
ssa_years <- c(1920:1929, 1970:1979, 2010:2019)
ssa_archive_files <- paste0("yob", ssa_years, ".txt")
ssa_extract_directory <- tempfile("barkonomics-ssa-")
dir.create(ssa_extract_directory)
unzip("data/raw/ssa-names.zip", files = ssa_archive_files, exdir = ssa_extract_directory)
ssa_file_paths <- file.path(ssa_extract_directory, ssa_archive_files)
ssa_raw <- read_csv(
  ssa_file_paths,
  col_names = c("name", "sex", "births"),
  col_types = cols(name = col_character(), sex = col_character(), births = col_integer()),
  id = "source_file", na = character()
)
ssa_raw |>
  problems() |>
  nrow() -> ssa_parsing_problem_count
stopifnot(ssa_parsing_problem_count == 0)
ssa_raw |>
  mutate(
    source_filename = basename(source_file),
    name_key = str_to_upper(name, locale = "en")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    year = str_extract(source_filename, "[0-9]{4}"),
    name_key = str_remove_all(name_key, "[\\s-]")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    year = as.integer(year),
    decade = (year %/% 10L) * 10L
  ) |>
  select(name_key, sex, year, decade, births) ->
  ssa_yearly
ssa_yearly |>
  distinct(year) |>
  pull(year) |>
  setequal(ssa_years) -> ssa_years_match_selection
stopifnot(ssa_years_match_selection)
ssa_yearly |>
  filter(births < 5) |>
  nrow() -> ssa_rows_below_publication_threshold
stopifnot(ssa_rows_below_publication_threshold == 0)
ssa_yearly |>
  count(name_key, sex, year, name = "records_in_group") |>
  filter(records_in_group > 1) |>
  nrow() -> duplicated_annual_name_count
stopifnot(duplicated_annual_name_count == 0)
```

### Rank names within decades
Sum across years and both SSA sex categories, then rank within each decade. Alphabetical name order breaks equal counts reproducibly, keeping exactly 100 names per decade. Shares use published SSA counts; suppressed names are absent from that denominator.

```{r}
#| label: rank-names-within-decades
ssa_yearly |>
  group_by(name_key, decade) |>
  summarise(births = sum(births), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(decade) |>
  arrange(desc(births), name_key, .by_group = TRUE, .locale = "C") |>
  mutate(rank = row_number(), share = births / sum(births), top100 = rank <= 100L) |>
  ungroup() ->
  ssa_decades
```

```{r}
#| label: rank-names-within-decades-preview
ssa_decades |>
  filter(rank <= 5)
```

### Make one reference row per name
Pivot before joining so a name appearing in several decades still has only one reference row. A missing decade has zero published births/share and no rank, rather than an invented rank.

```{r}
#| label: make-one-reference-row-per-name
ssa_decades |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = decade, values_from = c(births, share, rank, top100),
    values_fill = list(births = 0L, share = 0, top100 = FALSE)
  ) |>
  mutate(ssa_recognized = TRUE) |>
  arrange(name_key, .locale = "C") ->
  ssa_reference
ssa_reference |>
  count(name_key, name = "records_in_group") |>
  filter(records_in_group > 1) |>
  nrow() -> duplicated_reference_name_count
stopifnot(duplicated_reference_name_count == 0)
```

### Join name flags onto dogs
```{r}
#| label: join-name-flags-onto-dogs
name_flags <- c("ssa_recognized", "top100_1920", "top100_1970", "top100_2010")
ssa_reference |>
  select(name_key, all_of(name_flags)) ->
  ssa_name_flags

dogs_estimated |>
  left_join(
    ssa_name_flags,
    by = "name_key", relationship = "many-to-one", na_matches = "never"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    ssa_recognized = replace_na(ssa_recognized, FALSE),
    top100_1920 = replace_na(top100_1920, FALSE),
    top100_1970 = replace_na(top100_1970, FALSE),
    top100_2010 = replace_na(top100_2010, FALSE)
  ) |>
  select(
    estimated_dog_id, source_row_id, extract_year, name_original, name_key,
    sex, birth_year, breed, zipcode_original, zipcode,
    license_issue_date, license_expiry_date, license_record_count,
    original_name_variants, latest_issue_ties, compound_name, any_compound_name,
    breed_unknown, birth_year_suspect, sex_unknown, zipcode_padded, zipcode_invalid,
    identity_uncertain, all_of(name_flags)
  ) ->
  dogs
dogs |>
  nrow() -> matched_dog_count
dogs_estimated |>
  nrow() -> estimated_dog_count
stopifnot(matched_dog_count == estimated_dog_count)
dogs |>
  count(name_key, sex, birth_year, breed, zipcode, name = "records_in_group") |>
  filter(records_in_group > 1) |>
  nrow() -> duplicated_dog_count
stopifnot(duplicated_dog_count == 0)
dogs |>
  summarise(total = sum(license_record_count)) |>
  pull(total) -> represented_license_count
dogs_named |>
  nrow() -> named_license_count
stopifnot(represented_license_count == named_license_count)
```

```{r}
#| label: join-name-flags-onto-dogs-preview
dogs |>
  select(name_original, all_of(name_flags)) |>
  slice_head(n = 6)
```

### Trace source records to dogs
Keep a row-by-row explanation of which source records were consolidated or lacked a name.

```{r}
#| label: trace-source-records-to-dogs
dogs |>
  select(all_of(dog_key), estimated_dog_id, retained_source_row_id = source_row_id) ->
  dog_identity_lookup

dogs_clean |>
  left_join(
    dog_identity_lookup,
    by = dog_key, relationship = "many-to-one", na_matches = "never"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    record_status = case_when(
      name_missing ~ "missing_name",
      source_row_id == retained_source_row_id ~ "retained",
      TRUE ~ "consolidated"
    )
  ) |>
  select(source_row_id, estimated_dog_id, retained_source_row_id, record_status) ->
  license_to_dog
license_to_dog |>
  nrow() -> audited_license_count
stopifnot(audited_license_count == source_dog_record_count)
license_to_dog |>
  filter(record_status == "missing_name") |>
  nrow() -> audited_missing_name_count
dogs_clean |>
  filter(name_missing) |>
  nrow() -> source_missing_name_count
stopifnot(audited_missing_name_count == source_missing_name_count)
```

### Summarize source missingness
Missingness uses source license records, not the estimated-dog count.

```{r}
#| label: summarize-source-missingness
dogs_clean |>
  group_by(extract_year, zipcode) |>
  summarise(
    source_license_records = n(), missing_name_records = sum(name_missing),
    named_license_records = sum(!name_missing),
    missing_name_share = mean(name_missing), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(zipcode) ->
  missing_by_zip

dogs_clean |>
  filter(name_missing) |>
  count(name_original, name = "source_license_records", sort = TRUE) ->
  missing_name_counts
```

```{r}
#| label: summarize-source-missingness-preview
missing_name_counts
```

### Summarize quality flags
```{r}
#| label: summarize-quality-flags
quality_flags <- c("breed_unknown", "birth_year_suspect", "sex_unknown",
  "zipcode_padded", "zipcode_invalid", "identity_uncertain", "compound_name")
dogs_named |>
  summarise(across(all_of(quality_flags), sum)) |>
  mutate(unit = "named_license_record") ->
  license_quality_counts

dogs |>
  summarise(across(all_of(quality_flags), sum)) |>
  mutate(unit = "estimated_dog") ->
  dog_quality_counts

license_quality_counts |>
  bind_rows(dog_quality_counts) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(quality_flags), names_to = "flag", values_to = "count") |>
  select(unit, flag, count) ->
  quality_summary
```

```{r}
#| label: summarize-quality-flags-preview
quality_summary
```

### Inspect the top-100 cutoff
Inspect the 100/101 boundary instead of hiding a tie that could change list membership.

```{r}
#| label: inspect-the-top-100-cutoff
ssa_decades |>
  filter(rank %in% c(100L, 101L)) |>
  select(decade, rank, name_key, births) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = rank, values_from = c(name_key, births)) |>
  mutate(cutoff_tied = births_100 == births_101) ->
  ssa_cutoffs
```

### Compare counting units
This comparison shows the effect of record weighting without doing the later income analysis.

```{r}
#| label: compare-counting-units
dogs |>
  summarise(across(all_of(name_flags), mean)) |>
  mutate(unit = "estimated_dog") ->
  dog_matching_rates

dogs |>
  summarise(
    ssa_recognized = weighted.mean(ssa_recognized, license_record_count),
    top100_1920 = weighted.mean(top100_1920, license_record_count),
    top100_1970 = weighted.mean(top100_1970, license_record_count),
    top100_2010 = weighted.mean(top100_2010, license_record_count)
  ) |>
  mutate(unit = "named_license_record") ->
  license_matching_rates

dog_matching_rates |>
  bind_rows(license_matching_rates) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(name_flags), names_to = "measure", values_to = "share") |>
  select(unit, measure, share) ->
  matching_comparison
```

### Reconcile stage counts
```{r}
#| label: reconcile-stage-counts
stage_counts <- tribble(
  ~stage, ~count,
  "source_license_records", nrow(dogs_raw),
  "after_missing_label_join", nrow(dogs_clean),
  "missing_name_records", sum(dogs_clean$name_missing),
  "named_license_records", nrow(dogs_named),
  "estimated_dogs_before_ssa_join", nrow(dogs_estimated),
  "dogs_after_ssa_join", nrow(dogs),
  "consolidated_license_records", nrow(dogs_named) - nrow(dogs),
  "license_audit_rows", nrow(license_to_dog),
  "ssa_selected_year_rows", nrow(ssa_yearly),
  "ssa_name_decade_rows", nrow(ssa_decades),
  "ssa_reference_names", nrow(ssa_reference),
  "ssa_recognized_dogs", sum(dogs$ssa_recognized),
  "top100_1920_dogs", sum(dogs$top100_1920),
  "top100_1970_dogs", sum(dogs$top100_1970),
  "top100_2010_dogs", sum(dogs$top100_2010),
  "identity_uncertain_dogs", sum(dogs$identity_uncertain),
  "compound_name_dogs", sum(dogs$compound_name),
  "baby_source_records", sum(dogs_named$name_original == "BABY"),
  "baby_estimated_dogs", sum(dogs$name_original == "BABY")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: save-the-derived-tables
write_csv(dogs, "data/derived/dogs_2024.csv", na = "")
write_csv(ssa_reference, "data/derived/ssa_name_reference.csv", na = "")
write_csv(ssa_decades, "data/derived/ssa_name_decades.csv", na = "")
write_csv(license_to_dog, "data/derived/license_to_dog.csv", na = "")
write_csv(missing_by_zip, "data/derived/missing_names_by_zip.csv", na = "")
write_csv(missing_name_counts, "data/derived/missing_name_labels.csv", na = "")
write_csv(quality_summary, "data/derived/quality_flags.csv", na = "")
write_csv(ssa_cutoffs, "data/derived/ssa_top100_cutoffs.csv", na = "")

print(stage_counts, n = Inf)
print(ssa_cutoffs)
```

## Check the saved outputs
These checks read the CSV files again so they test the saved deliverable, not just the preparation objects in memory. They verify source coverage, five-field agreement, latest-license selection, missing-name treatment and the SSA matching flags. Run this section after preparation; it uses the `tidyverse` loaded in the setup chunk.

### Read the saved files
```{r}
#| label: read-the-saved-files
source_licenses <- read_csv(
  "data/raw/nyc-dogs-2024.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
  na = character(), trim_ws = FALSE
) |>
  mutate(source_row_id = row_number()) |>
  rename(zipcode_source = zipcode)

missing_labels <- read_csv(
  "data/lookups/missing_name_labels.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), na = character()
)

dog_handoff <- read_csv(
  "data/derived/dogs_2024.csv", na = "",
  col_types = cols(
    birth_year = col_character(),
    zipcode_original = col_character(),
    zipcode = col_character(),
    license_issue_date = col_date(),
    license_expiry_date = col_date(),
    .default = col_guess()
  )
)

license_audit <- read_csv("data/derived/license_to_dog.csv", na = "", show_col_types = FALSE)
ssa_reference <- read_csv("data/derived/ssa_name_reference.csv", na = "", show_col_types = FALSE)
ssa_decades <- read_csv("data/derived/ssa_name_decades.csv", na = "", show_col_types = FALSE)
missing_by_zip <- read_csv(
  "data/derived/missing_names_by_zip.csv", na = "",
  col_types = cols(zipcode = col_character(), .default = col_guess())
)
```

### Prepare the identity lookup
Give each lookup a name so its columns and row unit can be inspected before joining.

```{r}
#| label: prepare-the-identity-lookup
dog_handoff |>
  select(
    estimated_dog_id, name_key, sex, birth_year, breed, zipcode,
    license_issue_date, license_expiry_date
  ) ->
  dog_identity_lookup
```

### Compare source and saved identities
Trace every source license to its representative and compare the five identifying fields.

```{r}
#| label: compare-source-and-saved-identities
source_licenses |>
  left_join(license_audit, by = "source_row_id", relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  left_join(
    dog_identity_lookup,
    by = "estimated_dog_id", relationship = "many-to-one", na_matches = "never"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    source_name_missing = animalname %in% missing_labels$recorded_name,
    normalized_source_name = str_to_upper(animalname, locale = "en"),
    normalized_source_zip = str_pad(zipcode_source, width = 5, pad = "0"),
    source_issue_date = str_sub(licenseissueddate, 1, 10),
    source_expiry_date = str_sub(licenseexpireddate, 1, 10)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    normalized_source_name = str_remove_all(normalized_source_name, "[\\s-]"),
    source_issue_date = as.Date(source_issue_date),
    source_expiry_date = as.Date(source_expiry_date),
    five_fields_agree = name_key == normalized_source_name & sex == animalgender &
      birth_year == animalbirth & breed == breedname & zipcode == normalized_source_zip
  ) ->
  mapped_licenses

mapped_licenses |>
  filter(!source_name_missing) ->
  named_licenses

mapped_licenses |>
  filter(source_name_missing) ->
  missing_licenses

mapped_licenses |>
  filter(record_status == "retained") ->
  retained_licenses
```

### Check representative selection and group sizes
No source license should outrank its retained representative under the documented tie rule.

```{r}
#| label: check-representative-selection-and-group-sizes
named_licenses |>
  mutate(
    later_issue = source_issue_date > license_issue_date,
    same_issue = source_issue_date == license_issue_date,
    later_expiry = source_expiry_date > license_expiry_date,
    same_expiry = source_expiry_date == license_expiry_date,
    earlier_source_row = source_row_id < retained_source_row_id,
    outranks_retained = later_issue | (same_issue & later_expiry) |
      (same_issue & same_expiry & earlier_source_row)
  ) ->
  license_selection

dog_handoff |>
  select(estimated_dog_id, license_record_count) ->
  dog_group_sizes

license_audit |>
  filter(!is.na(estimated_dog_id)) |>
  count(estimated_dog_id, name = "actual_license_count") |>
  left_join(dog_group_sizes, by = "estimated_dog_id", relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  mutate(counts_agree = actual_license_count == license_record_count) ->
  group_counts
```

### Compare saved name flags
Compare each saved matching flag with the reference, keeping the four comparisons visible.

```{r}
#| label: compare-saved-name-flags
flag_names <- c("ssa_recognized", "top100_1920", "top100_1970", "top100_2010")
ssa_reference |>
  select(name_key, all_of(flag_names)) ->
  reference_flags

dog_handoff |>
  select(estimated_dog_id, name_key, all_of(flag_names)) |>
  left_join(
    reference_flags, by = "name_key",
    relationship = "many-to-one", suffix = c("_dog", "_reference")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    recognition_agrees = ssa_recognized_dog == replace_na(ssa_recognized_reference, FALSE),
    decade_1920_agrees = top100_1920_dog == replace_na(top100_1920_reference, FALSE),
    decade_1970_agrees = top100_1970_dog == replace_na(top100_1970_reference, FALSE),
    decade_2010_agrees = top100_2010_dog == replace_na(top100_2010_reference, FALSE),
    all_flags_agree = recognition_agrees & decade_1920_agrees &
      decade_1970_agrees & decade_2010_agrees
  ) ->
  flag_checks

ssa_decades |>
  filter(top100) |>
  count(decade, name = "name_count") ->
  top100_counts

named_licenses |>
  filter(animalname == "BABY") ->
  baby_licenses

named_licenses |>
  filter(breedname == "Unknown") ->
  unknown_breed_licenses

dog_handoff |>
  select(breed_unknown, birth_year_suspect, sex_unknown, zipcode_invalid, identity_uncertain) |>
  mutate(
    expected_uncertainty = breed_unknown | birth_year_suspect | sex_unknown | zipcode_invalid,
    flag_agrees = identity_uncertain == expected_uncertainty
  ) ->
  uncertainty_flags

dog_handoff |>
  select(all_of(flag_names)) ->
  saved_name_flags
```

### Run the saved-file checks
Each row pairs a check's description with its result, rather than keeping two parallel lists.

```{r}
#| label: run-the-saved-file-checks
checks <- tribble(
  ~check, ~passed,
  "105974 source rows",
  nrow(source_licenses) == 105974,
  "audit covers every source row exactly once",
  nrow(license_audit) == nrow(source_licenses) &&
    setequal(license_audit$source_row_id, source_licenses$source_row_id) &&
    !anyDuplicated(license_audit$source_row_id),
  "dog IDs unique",
  !anyDuplicated(dog_handoff$estimated_dog_id),
  "five-field dog keys unique",
  !anyDuplicated(dog_handoff[c("name_key", "sex", "birth_year", "breed", "zipcode")]),
  "source names classified before normalization",
  all(is.na(mapped_licenses$estimated_dog_id) == mapped_licenses$source_name_missing),
  "5810 missing-name records excluded only from name analysis",
  nrow(missing_licenses) == 5810 && all(missing_licenses$record_status == "missing_name"),
  "all named rows assigned",
  !anyNA(named_licenses$estimated_dog_id),
  "one retained row per estimated dog",
  nrow(retained_licenses) == nrow(dog_handoff) && !anyDuplicated(retained_licenses$estimated_dog_id),
  "retained IDs agree with dog CSV",
  setequal(retained_licenses$source_row_id, dog_handoff$source_row_id),
  "group sizes reconcile",
  all(group_counts$counts_agree) && sum(dog_handoff$license_record_count) == nrow(named_licenses),
  "latest license and deterministic ties",
  !any(license_selection$outranks_retained),
  "all five key fields agree",
  all(named_licenses$five_fields_agree),
  "ZIP codes are five-character text",
  is.character(dog_handoff$zipcode) && all(str_detect(dog_handoff$zipcode, "^[0-9]{5}$")),
  "source missingness reconciles by ZIP",
  sum(missing_by_zip$source_license_records) == nrow(source_licenses) &&
    sum(missing_by_zip$missing_name_records) == nrow(missing_licenses),
  "reference names unique",
  !anyDuplicated(ssa_reference$name_key),
  "100 names in each selected decade",
  setequal(top100_counts$decade, c(1920, 1970, 2010)) && all(top100_counts$name_count == 100),
  "dog/reference flags agree",
  all(flag_checks$all_flags_agree),
  "unmatched and recognized dogs retained",
  any(dog_handoff$ssa_recognized) && any(!dog_handoff$ssa_recognized) && !anyNA(saved_name_flags),
  "BABY source records retained",
  nrow(baby_licenses) == 120 && !anyNA(baby_licenses$estimated_dog_id),
  "uncertain records retained",
  nrow(unknown_breed_licenses) == 8287 && !anyNA(unknown_breed_licenses$estimated_dog_id),
  "uncertainty flags are complete and consistent",
  !anyNA(uncertainty_flags) && all(uncertainty_flags$flag_agrees)
)
write_csv(checks, "data/derived/validation_checks.csv")
print(checks, n = Inf)
checks |>
  pull(passed) |>
  all() -> all_checks_passed
stopifnot(all_checks_passed)
```

### Record runtime versions
rowwise() looks up one package version at a time; ungroup() returns an ordinary table.

```{r}
#| label: record-runtime-versions
getRversion() |>
  as.character() ->
  r_version

tibble(package = "R", version = r_version) -> r_runtime
tibble(package = c("tidyverse", "dplyr", "readr", "stringr", "tidyr")) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(version = as.character(packageVersion(package))) |>
  ungroup() ->
  package_versions

r_runtime |>
  bind_rows(package_versions) ->
  runtime
write_csv(runtime, "data/derived/runtime_versions.csv")
```

## Decisions and limitations
- Classify the six exact missing-name labels through the [lookup](data/lookups/missing_name_labels.csv) before normalization. Keep `BABY` and all other recorded names; unmatched names remain in the named denominator.
- Normalize complete names by uppercasing and removing spaces/hyphens; preserve original strings and compound flags.
- Group by normalized full name, recorded sex, recorded birth year, recorded breed and five-character ZIP. Keep latest issue date, then latest expiry date, then smallest source row number. There are 773 groups with tied latest issue dates, handled deterministically. No normalization-induced multiple-original-name group occurs in this snapshot.
- Keep unknown breeds and suspect birth years as recorded, with flags. There are 7,732 estimated dogs with unknown breed and 42 with suspect birth year; their union contains 7,771 dogs. The 1990–2024 birth-year range is a review screen, not an exclusion. Unknown breed offers less identity evidence; a false uncertainty flag does not prove identity either.
- Restore leading zeros on 40 digit-only source ZIP values. All resulting ZIPs have five digits, but syntax alone says nothing about NYC membership, crosswalk coverage or income availability.
- Recognize names appearing in any published SSA record in the selected thirty years, combining SSA sex categories. For decade lists, sum counts across years and sex, order by count descending and name alphabetically, and keep exactly 100. None of the observed rank-100/rank-101 boundaries is tied.
- Allow names to match multiple decades. Build one wide reference row per normalized name before joining, so overlap never multiplies dog rows.

Identity remains approximate. Different dogs can share all five fields, and a dog whose recorded attributes change can remain in several groups. [The record-weighted comparison](data/derived/matching_by_counting_unit.csv) gives SSA recognition of 78.78%, compared with 78.65% for estimated dogs. That small citywide difference does not establish that the effect is small in each neighborhood.

SSA recognition is limited to published names in the chosen periods, including suppression of low counts and incomplete early coverage. It is not a universal human-name test. Ranks and shares refer to combined-sex counts; a dog's sex does not restrict matching.
